newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - PT Dharmala sets flexible FRN.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - PT Dharmala sets flexible FRN.

text.p: Asian debt markets offered a couple of new issues on Monday, including an unusually styled deal for an Indonesian conglomerate.
Peregrine Fixed Income launched a US$100 million floating rate note issue for Dharmala Inti Utama International BV, a wholly owned subsidiary of Dharmala Inti Utama, which guarantees the issue.
The notes have a final maturity of three years but can be put at the second anniversary.

The notes were launched without a set coupon rate. Rather, the rate will be set by market demand within certain parameters, in this case 265 to 300 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
The idea is for the spread to be a reflection of market demand for a credit rather than the result of competition among banks for the mandate.
Potential participants have until September 20 to submit commitments and the lowest coupons they will accept.

"In most deals in Asia, the arrangers decide on a coupon and investors can take it or leave it. What we want to do is establish the appropriate coupon so the issuer will be happy and the investor will be happy," said a syndicate manager at Peregrine Fixed Income.
If the price is right, there will be better liquidity in the secondary market without wild swings in prices, he said.
The long syndication period with flexible pricing is similar to Euro-style roadshows, where investor interest shapes the final price and lead managers can assess demand.
But formal presentations for Dharmala were held last week.
Fees are a flat 100 basis points regardless of participation level, giving an all-in return of 315 to 350 basis points to the put option.
Lead managers receive additional fees in the form of undisclosed underwriting and selling fees, as in bond-style syndications, to encourage selling.
Peregrine syndicated an FRN issue for Asia Pulp and Paper in the same way last June.
Elsewhere, Union Bank of Hong Kong set a US$50 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue via arrangers Bayerische Landesbank, which will handle books, and Jardine Fleming Bank.

The certificates mature in five years but can be put or called on the third and fourth anniversaries. The deal pays a margin of 45 basis points over three-month LIBOR and with fees an all-in return of 66 basis points to the top tier.
Looking ahead, KEXIM is expected to launch a US$500 million five-year bond shortly. Nomura and SBC Warburg are the leads.
Other Asian borrower seen tapping the Eurobond markets soon are the Philippines PCIBank, via Merrill Lynch, and Indonesia's Mulia Land, through J.P. Morgan.
In other debt news, the International Finance Corp, an affiliate of the World Bank, plans to set up a credit enhancement agency to promote the issue of bonds for Asian infrastructure projects.
The new agency will be called Global Gurantee Association (GGA) and is expected to be established by year-end.
The Asian Development Bank already has created a credit enhancement agency called Asia Ltd.
